## Views of the list (Alt+V)

**Alt+V** opens other ways to look at the files of the list (the directory,
Branch or Showall, with the filespec and `W` that are on). They only read:
what you choose in one goes back to the file window as a filter, and from
there Ctrl+T, Ctrl+C or Batch act as always.

- **Scan (`S`):** what in a folder deserves a look before you open it. Names
  with hidden characters or a double extension (`fatura.pdf.exe`), setuid
  files and what anyone can write, links that leave the folder or point to
  nothing, and, read with the viewer's own readers and limits, executables
  without PIE or NX or packed, Office documents with macros or a remote
  template, patches that climb out with `..`. Enter on a category brings its
  files back to the list. It is not an antivirus: it points, it does not
  promise the rest is safe.
- **Timeline (`T`):** the files in a histogram by the date they changed, by
  hours, days, weeks, months or years. Enter on a bar, or on a range
  (Shift+← →), keeps only its files, as a `W` condition.
- **Table (`L`):** the list in the table viewer, a file per row with the
  columns of `W` (`name`, `ext`, `dir`, `size`, `modified`, `age_days`,
  `mode`...). It has the SQL filter, the record as a form and Batch, and a
  list of millions of files opens at once. **W** there takes the filter back
  to the file window as its condition.

## Fuzzy find (`|`)

Type pieces of a name (`cfgxy` finds `config/xylem`, `rdme` finds
`README.md`) and the cursor goes to the best folder in the tree, or the best
file in the file window. The results show as you type, the best first, even
in a tree of millions of folders. Ctrl+T tags the chosen result and Alt+T the
whole list. A new page of the manual, "Finding files and folders", says which
search answers which question.

## Ebooks

EPUB and FictionBook (`.fb2`, `.fb2.zip`) open as a book to read, in a
column with the paragraphs of a printed book: a title page, Space for the
next page, `]` `[` for chapters, Tab for the contents, Enter for the notes
called on the page, `g 40%` for a part of the book, and how long is left of
the chapter and of the book. `I` shows the report on the file: what the book
says of itself, and whether it carries scripts, things fetched from outside
or DRM.

`R` remembers where you stopped, and the book opens there next time. If you
turn it on (F12, page 5), Xylem also keeps the time you spent reading each
book, your sessions and your reading speed, only on your computer.

## Norton Guides

The viewer reads **Norton Guides** (`.ng`), the help files of DOS and Clipper
libraries. V or Autoview shows a guide as a document: its title and credits,
its menus, then every entry with a number (`§12`). Links and see-also lines
say which entry they lead to (`→ §12`). **Tab** chooses a link, **Enter** (or
a click) follows it and **Backspace** goes back; the viewer's search still
looks through the whole guide. The drawing characters of the guide show as
they did in DOS. A guide that is damaged or made to trick a reader shows what
it can, with a list of the problems at the top. H shows the bytes.

The format is known thanks to Dave Pearson, who worked it out in the 1990s:
https://www.davep.org/norton-guides/

## New versions

Xylem can tell that a new version is out. The first time it starts, it asks
whether it may look once a day; with a yes, it fetches only the number of the
latest version from the website, and the top line says when a newer one is
out. Nothing is downloaded or installed, and **G** on page 3 of F12 changes
the answer later.

## Smaller things

- **F1** opens the help at the section of what you are doing (in the Batch of
  the viewer, at "Batch in the viewer"), and links to a section of a page now
  lead to it.
- `O` in the viewer goes through two more encodings, Windows-1251 and KOI8-R
  (Cyrillic), before UTF-16.
- The Type display (Alt+F) says `EPUB ebook (ZIP)`, `FB2 ebook` and
  `FB2 ebook (ZIP)`.

## Fixed

- With Git on, a big repository on a slow file system (`/mnt/c` from WSL, a
  network share) froze the screen while `git status` ran, for minutes. The
  status is now read in the background, and a slow repository is read again
  less often.
- The library Xylem uses for system calls (rustix 1.1.6) is updated for an
  advisory about extended attributes
  ([RUSTSEC-2026-0486](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0486)).
